title: Loose Rein plan.yaml (rein-grounded-v1)
description: The Expected Model: what this cycle claims the implementation will do, and the task DAG that builds it. Frozen at gate 3. Three sections and no more — `claims` ties each R-N/NFR-N heading of docs/10-requirements.md to a statement, `tasks` ties each statement to the work that answers it, and `rein dag --trace` walks the thread end to end. Every enum here is mirrored by a constant in rein/models.py; tests/test_models.py fails if the two drift.

repoPath.description: A repo-relative POSIX path. No absolute form, no '..' segment, no backslash — a reference that can escape the repository is not a reference to anything reviewable.

claim.description: What one requirement means, in a sentence a reviewer can hold against the code. `requirement_ids` is what makes it traceable: a claim citing an id no heading declares is a dangling reference, and a heading no claim cites is an uncovered requirement — `rein dag --trace` blocks on both.

kind.description: The DAG role that drives orchestration: layers, parallelism, and merge order derive from it, not from LLM discretion.

scope.description: Where this task's work belongs. Each entry covers the path it names and everything beneath it; a trailing '/' is optional punctuation and changes nothing, and the prefix is anchored at a separator (`src/app` covers `src/app/x.py`, never `src/app.py`). An empty `include` is unbounded, not forbidden. Checked against the real diff by the build loop.

acceptance.description: This task's own bar, in a form something can check. Acceptance criteria used to live only as markdown checkboxes in `docs/tasks/T-NNN.md`, which nothing parsed — so 'the acceptance criteria are met' was an assertion by the agent that wrote the code. Stating them here does NOT let a task pick its own quality gate: the shared DoD in config.yaml still runs, unchanged, and this list is frozen by a human at gate ③ exactly like everything else in the plan.

operator_surface.description: What this task will require of a person: a setting somebody has to supply, a schema somebody has to migrate, a dependency somebody has to provide, a signal somebody has to watch. Frozen at gate 3 with the rest of the task, which is what turns it into an Expected side — at gate 4 the blind extractor's readings are sorted by whether one of these foresaw them, and the readings nothing foresaw are what the approver is shown first. Declaring nothing is allowed; it means every operator-facing reading in that area arrives at gate 4 as undeclared.

kind.description: A subset of the Actual Statement categories in review.schema.json, not a vocabulary of its own: the declaration is compared against what a blind extractor read out of the code, and two vocabularies over one comparison would need a mapping table that can be wrong. These are the categories describing a surface somebody outside the code can see.

name.description: What a person deals with, in their words — a settings key, a table and column, a queue, an endpoint. Never matched against anything: prose compared to prose is the overclaim the gate 4 brief exists to avoid, so `paths` is what carries the comparison.

paths.description: Where this surface can be read at the reviewed commit — the migration, the schema file, the settings module. Covered the same way `scope` is (the path it names and everything beneath it, trailing slash optional), and this is what an extracted statement's code anchor is matched against. It is also what gate 4 offers as the as-built view: the file as it ends up, which a diff never shows.

adr.description: The decision record that settled what this requires of a person and whether it can be undone. Shown beside the declaration at gate 4 so the trade-off a human approved at gate 2 is reachable from what was built — the review never restates it, because a restatement is a sentence nobody observed.

statement.description: One criterion, stated so that it could be false.

evidence.description: How this criterion is established. Absent means it is prose only — most criteria are, and that is honest; it simply contributes no evidence and is left to the gate ④ review.

kind.description: `command` runs an argv in a sandboxed profile and is decided by exit status. `artifact` requires the named paths to exist. `external` is evidence this loop cannot obtain — a staging check, a device, a person — so a task carrying one reaches `awaiting-evidence` rather than `done`, and a human records the observation with `rein evidence record`.

command.description: An argv array, never a shell string — the same rule the quality gate follows, for the same reason.
